## Adapting This Course

::: {.section-intro}
This course is designed to be adopted and adapted by Higher Education Institutions worldwide.
Everything here — sessions, slides, frameworks, assessment designs — is published under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
You are free to take what you need, leave what you don't, and build something better, for non-commercial
purposes and under the same license.
This page explains how.
:::

---

::: {.adapt-grid}

::: {.adapt-card}
### 1. Use individual sessions

You do not need to run the whole course. Any session can stand alone as a guest lecture,
workshop module, or seminar input. Each session page is self-contained with learning objectives,
materials, tasks, and a localisation note.

**How**: Download the session QMD file from GitHub, or copy the content into your own course design.
:::

::: {.adapt-card}
### 2. Swap in local case studies

Every session includes a **localisation note** — a yellow panel at the bottom of the page —
that guides you on how to replace our default examples (often European or generic global)
with cases from your own regional context.

**How**: Follow the localisation note. If you develop a strong local example, please share it
via a GitHub pull request so other institutions can benefit.
:::

::: {.adapt-card}
### 3. Translate

All materials are licensed for translation. A German version is in preparation at CDE.
If you translate materials into another language, please notify the course team so we can
link to your version from the repository.

**How**: Fork the GitHub repository, edit the QMD files, and publish your translated version.
:::

::: {.adapt-card}
### 4. Remix and extend

Add sessions, change the sequence, integrate your own assessments, or embed this course within
a larger programme. The Quarto format makes structural edits straightforward.

**How**: Fork the repository. The `_quarto.yml` navigation and `sessions/index.qmd` listing
control the structure. `_variables.yml` lets you update course metadata in one place.
:::

::: {.adapt-card}
### 5. Run a co-taught version

This course was designed for co-teaching across institutions. The Session 04 presentations are
especially powerful when run jointly between partner institutions via video link.

**How**: Contact the CDE coordination team at [cde@unibe.ch](mailto:cde@unibe.ch) to discuss
scheduling a joint cohort with another partner institution.
:::

::: {.adapt-card}
### 6. Contribute back

The course improves when institutions share what they changed and why. Contributions welcome:
new case studies, updated readings, improved localisation notes, translations, additional sessions.

**How**: Open an issue or pull request on the [GitHub repository]({{< var course.github >}}).
All contributors are acknowledged in the repository's commit history and contributor list.
:::

:::

---

## Technical Setup

The course is built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org) — an open-source scientific publishing system.
You need Quarto installed to render the site locally.

**Quick start:**

```bash
# 1. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/CDEteaching/[REPO-NAME].git
cd [REPO-NAME]

# 2. Install Quarto (see https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/)

# 3. Preview locally
quarto preview

# 4. Render to _site/ folder
quarto render
```

Deployment to GitHub Pages is automated via the included GitHub Actions workflow
(`.github/workflows/publish.yml`). Push to `main` and the site rebuilds automatically.

**Editing in RStudio**: Open the project folder in RStudio — it will detect the Quarto project
automatically. Use the Render button to preview individual pages.
